The Inherit the Winds TV anime is inspired by the first story in the popular Tachikawa Jinsuke stage play tetralogy performed by the theatre group Caramel Box since 1996. Filmmaker Zach Cregger has another big hit on his hands with the successful launch of Resident Evil. Amid the new film's success, fans may be wondering how his Batman movie would have turned out if it had gotten made.
...
During a new interview for Men's Health, Cregger shared details about Henchman, his screenplay for a film set in Gotham City. It came with a unique twist, as while characters like Batman and The Joker were present, they were not the focus. The film would have instead focused on an everyman who happens to get caught up in a conflict between the Dark Knight and the Clown Prince of Crime. This is reminiscent of the new Resident Evil following a courier who stumbles into Raccoon City right when the zombie outbreak from the games begins, rather than using a powerful and established character.
...
“It’s about a normal guy," Cregger said of the script, which was the first movie screenplay he ever wrote. "It’s about a pharmacist who lives in Gotham City, and he gets accidentally sucked into this incredible power play between Batman and The Joker. And he finds himself a very integral part of something. And so, it’s a weird movie. It’s someone living on the periphery of all the stories in Gotham that we know of, and it’s about some rando. I’m not the world’s biggest Batman guy at all, but I just liked this story. I liked this character. I liked what happened to him, so it was just fun.”
...
Most comic book movies focus on popular superheroes, although some will shift the focus to villains, with characters like The Joker and Clayface getting their own movies. What's very uncommon is for a movie based on DC or Marvel comic books to keep the focus on a "normal guy" and turning the superheroes and supervillains into side characters. As the movie was not made and Cregger has moved on to other projects, it seems improbable that Henchman will ever see the light of day, though the director's fans can imagine how it might have turned out.
...

The Savage Sword of Conan: The Original Comics Omnibus Vol. 8 Conan the Barbarian has just made his triumphant return with an exciting new release perfect for fans of the sword-and-sorcery icon. A stunning eighth new omnibus is now on sale from Titan Comics.
The Savage Sword of Conan: The Original Comics Omnibus Vol.8 was released on Sept. 8 with over one thousand pages of digitally remastered artwork and a host of bonus material. The high-quality release collects Savage Sword of Conan (1974) #102-116 as well as Marvel Comics Super Special (1977) #35 in a beautiful and deluxe hardcover format. It picks up the story directly from where the seventh omnibus left off, so Conan fans looking to complete their collection will definitely want to pick up the new release, which has a suggested retail price of $150.
Renowned Conan the Barbarian Illustrator Returns for New Omnibus Release
Titan and Penguin Random House's listing for the Original Comics Omnibus Vol. 8 promises unseen bonus material, a section of "rarely seen artwork" as well as an all-new introduction from Conan comics legend, Gary Kwapisz. Known for his detailed artwork that brought some of Conan's most savage scenes to life, Kwapisz worked not only on The Savage Sword of Conan but also Titan Comics released a deluxe hardcover omnibus collecting Savage Sword of Conan #102‑116 and Marvel Super Special #35 on Sept. 2026 World Webtoon Awards Announces 20 Finalists, Opens Global Reader Vote Korea's Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism (MCST) and the Korea Creative Content Agency (KOCCA) announced on Thursday the 20 finalists for the 2026 World Webtoon Awards.
Now in their third year, the awards will accept online votes from readers worldwide from September 17 to October 19. Judges' scores and reader votes will each account for 50% of the final score.
This year's awards received 7,318 nominations from 4,038 fans worldwide, with 941 works submitted in total.
For the first time, the awards will also offer cash prizes. The grand prize winner will receive 15 million won (about US$10,700), while the Judges' Award winner will receive 13 million won (about US$9,400) and other main award winners will receive 10 million won (about US$7,200) each.
The awards ceremony will take place on December 3 at Starfield Library in COEX Mall, Seoul, as part of the World Webtoon Festival, which runs from December 2 to 6.

Tetsu Kariya and Akira Hanasaki’s long-running Oishinbo cooking manga series is receiving a new TV anime adaptation titled Shin Oishinbo. The new anime project was announced during a stage event at ABEMA Anime Festival 2026 celebrating Shin-Ei Animation’s 50th anniversary.
...
The Oishinbo manga series, which is written by Kariya and drawn by Hanasaki, has been serialized in Shogakukan’s Big Comic Spirits magazine since October 1983. It has been in an indefinite hiatus since May 2014. A total of 111 tankobon volumes have been published in Japan as of December 2014.
...
The manga previously inspired a TV anime series from Shin-Ei Animation from 1988 to 1992, as well as two anime films from Studio Deen in 1992 and 1993, respectively. A live-action film adaptation was also released in 1996. The long-running Oishinbo cooking manga will receive a new TV anime adaptation titled Shin Oishinbo.
